director.question: q0
director.why: q0 offers the highest expected information at 0.079 bits and directly tests continued rise versus post-peak fade.

question.text: Brighter in r three days from now than at its last r detection?

payload.rule: Every ZTF g or r measurement taken after this bet was sealed, up to one day past its last forecast, is scored against the forecast, interpolated linearly between days. The question is settled by the first r measurement within a day of its time; a limit above the reference leaves it void.

instrument.why: Multi-epoch, multi-band detections spanning ~16 days show coherent gradual brightening, not a single-night spike or erratic jumps.

implausible.why: Fitted peak 27 days ago requires post-peak fading during days -17 to -2 while r-band brightens by ~0.8 mag over 16 days, opposite to normal stripped-envelope decline.

Fitted peak 24 days ago requires post-peak plateau or decline during days -17 to -2 while r-band brightens by ~0.8 mag over 16 days, opposite to Type II post-peak behavior and too slow for a Type II r

Red observed color g-r ~0.6 and fitted temperature pegged at the 10000 K floor contradict the hot blue continuum required for a TDE and the ~995 day timescale is far longer than physical fallback time

theories.argument: The 16-day slow rise from g~20.4 and r~20.2 at -17.7d to g~20.0, r~19.36 and i~19.33 at -1.7d with reddening g-r color matches a broad reddened SN Ia at z=0.2 peaking at -4.4d. The Ia fit explains all detections and deep early limits with chi2 per point of 0.87 and the leading weight of 0.51.

refuted_if.why: The Ia model requires continued post-maximum fading well below the -1.7d level by +3d, so sustained brightness would rule out nickel-powered decline.

theories.weakest_point: The fit needs extreme broad and red parameters at the edge of the Ia distribution with x1=2.67 and c=0.42 and relies on sparse detections with marginal stamp reality p_real=0.627.

theories.argument: Deep limits from day -42 to -26 followed by faint emergence at -17.7 to -15.6 traces a stripped-envelope rise compatible with an Ib/c at z=0.158. The red colors with g-r ~0.3-0.6 and brighter i~19.3 at -1.7 fit the Ni-powered template with chi2/point 0.69 at high latitude with no host light.

refuted_if.why: At ~30 d after the fitted -27.4 d peak the Ib/c must be on a fading Co tail in g, so further brightening is incompatible.

theories.weakest_point: The fitted peak at -27.4 d makes the -17 to -1 detections 10 to 26 d post-peak yet they brighten in r from 20.2 to 19.36 instead of decaying, and the stamp is marginal at p_real=0.627.

theories.argument: Detections in g, r and i persist over ~16 days from day -17.7 to day -1.7 with red colors (g-r ~0.6 mag) and slow ~0.5 mag evolution, consistent with a long-lived plateau. This red, slowly evolving emission at the fitted z~0.15 is naturally produced by recombination in a hydrogen-rich envelope after core collapse.

refuted_if.why: A Type II plateau should remain near ~65 uJy in r for weeks, so a fade this deep would rule out plateau emission.

theories.weakest_point: The Type II fit carries only ~1% weight with chi2 ~2.2 per point and rests on sparse detections separated by ~7-day gaps with only a marginal stamp (p_real 0.63).

wording.text: It is unlikely that this object will look brighter in red light three days from now than it did in its last red-light measurement.
